# Coaching Cues Library

Proven coaching cues organized by movement pattern. Use these as your go-to toolkit and adapt them to each client's level.

---

## SQUAT (Back Squat, Front Squat, Goblet Squat, Wide Squat)

### Setup
- "Screw your feet into the floor" — creates external rotation torque, activates glutes.
- "Grab the floor with your toes" — anchors the feet and activates the arch.
- "Big breath into your belly, like you're inflating a balloon behind your belt buckle" — teaches proper bracing.

### Descent (Eccentric)
- "Sit back like there's a chair behind you" — prevents knees shooting forward.
- "Spread the floor apart with your feet" — keeps knees tracking over toes and fires glutes.
- "Pull yourself down with your hip flexors" — controls the eccentric speed.
- "Keep your chest facing the mirror in front of you" — prevents forward lean.

### Ascent (Concentric)
- **"Push the floor away from you"** — shifts focus from "standing up" to driving through the feet.
- "Drive your traps into the bar" — cues upper back tightness and upright torso.
- "Stand tall, like someone is pulling a string from the top of your head" — full lockout.

### Common Mistakes
- **Knees caving:** "Think about showing the logo on your shoes to the walls on each side."
- **Butt wink:** "Stop an inch before your pelvis tucks — own that depth, don't chase more."
- **Forward lean:** "Your nipples should point at the wall, not at the floor."

---

## DEADLIFT (Conventional, Sumo, Romanian, Stiff-Leg)

### Setup
- "Push your feet through the floor before the bar even moves" — pre-tensions the posterior chain.
- "Protect the oranges in your armpits — squeeze them tight" — engages lats.
- "Bend the bar around your shins" — activates lats and keeps bar close.

### Pull (Concentric)
- **"Push the earth away"** — mental shift from pulling to leg-driving.
- "Drag the bar up your legs like you're shaving them" — keeps bar path straight.
- "Hips and shoulders rise together like an elevator" — prevents hips shooting up first.
- "Stand tall and squeeze a coin between your glutes at the top" — cues hip extension lockout.

### Lowering (Eccentric)
- "Push your hips back like you're closing a car door with your butt" — RDL hinge pattern.
- "The bar slides down your thighs — it never leaves your body" — maintains bar contact.

### Common Mistakes
- **Rounded back:** "Imagine you have a broomstick taped to your spine — it should touch your head, upper back, and tailbone at all times."
- **Bar drifting forward:** "The bar is a paint roller — roll it up your legs."
- **Jerking the bar:** "Take the slack out first — you should hear the plates click before the bar leaves the ground."

---

## BENCH PRESS (Flat, Incline, Dumbbell)

### Setup
- "Pinch your shoulder blades together like you're holding a pencil between them" — creates a stable shelf.
- "Bend the bar into a U-shape" — activates lats and stabilizes shoulders.
- "Your feet should push you up the bench — leg drive is real" — teaches leg drive.

### Descent (Eccentric)
- "Pull the bar to your chest with your back, not just lower it" — active eccentric control.
- "Tuck your elbows at 45° — imagine you're making an arrow shape, not a T" — protects shoulders.

### Press (Concentric)
- **"Push yourself away from the bar into the bench"** — external focus that improves force output.
- "Drive the bar back toward the rack in a slight arc" — correct bar path.
- "Punch the ceiling" — cues explosive intent on dumbbell press.

### Common Mistakes
- **Flared elbows:** "Arrow, not a T — elbows at 45°."
- **Butt lifting:** "Your butt is glued to the bench — drive through your heels instead."
- **Bouncing off chest:** "One-second pause at the bottom — the chest is a shelf, not a trampoline."

---

## OVERHEAD PRESS (Barbell, Dumbbell, Push Press)

### Setup
- "Stack your wrists over your elbows — imagine a straight column from wrist to elbow" — efficient force transfer.
- "Squeeze your glutes and abs like someone's about to punch you in the stomach" — creates a rigid base.

### Press (Concentric)
- **"Push your head through the window"** — after the bar passes your face, push your head forward and look up.
- "Try to touch the ceiling with the bar" — cues full lockout.
- "Move your head around the bar, not the bar around your head" — efficient bar path.

### Common Mistakes
- **Excessive lean-back:** "You're pressing overhead, not doing a standing incline press — stay vertical."
- **Wrists bent back:** "Knuckles pointing at the ceiling."

---

## ROW (Barbell Row, Dumbbell Row, Cable Row)

### Setup
- "Hinge at the hips — your torso should look like a table top" — correct angle for barbell row.
- "Let your arms hang straight like ropes attached to the weight" — full stretch at bottom.

### Pull (Concentric)
- **"Drive your elbow to your back pocket"** — cues scapular retraction and lat engagement.
- "Pull with your elbows, not your hands — your hands are just hooks" — minimizes bicep dominance.
- "Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top like you're cracking a walnut between them" — peak contraction.

### Common Mistakes
- **Using momentum:** "If your torso moves more than 10°, the weight is too heavy."
- **Pulling to the chest instead of the hips:** "Aim for your belly button on barbell rows — that targets lats."

---

## PULL-UP / LAT PULLDOWN

### Execution
- **"Pull the bar to your chest by driving your elbows into your back pockets"** — external focus for lats.
- "Imagine you're bending the bar around your collarbone" — engages lats over arms.
- "Lead with your chest, not your chin" — prevents the chin-jutting cheat.
- "Squeeze your shoulder blades down and back before you pull — set the shoulders first" — scapular depression.

### Common Mistakes
- **Half reps:** "Dead hang at the bottom — earn each rep from a full stretch."
- **Kipping:** "If your legs are swinging, reduce the weight or use a band."

---

## HIP THRUST / GLUTE BRIDGE

### Execution
- **"Drive your heels through the floor and squeeze your glutes like you're cracking a walnut"** — maximal glute activation.
- "Your shins should be vertical at the top — like fence posts" — optimal knee angle.
- "Tuck your chin slightly — look at where the wall meets the ceiling" — prevents lumbar hyperextension.
- "Think about making your belt buckle touch the ceiling" — cues posterior pelvic tilt at top.

### Common Mistakes
- **Hyperextending the lower back:** "Stop when your body makes a straight line from knees to shoulders — no bridge arch."
- **Pushing through toes:** "Wiggle your toes at the top — if you can't, shift to your heels."

---

## LUNGE / SPLIT SQUAT / BULGARIAN SPLIT SQUAT

### Execution
- **"Drop your back knee straight down like an elevator, don't lunge forward"** — keeps shin vertical.
- "90-90: both knees make right angles at the bottom" — depth reference.
- "Keep your torso like a flagpole — straight up" — prevents forward lean.

### Common Mistakes
- **Knee shooting past toes:** "Your front shin stays vertical — imagine it's pressed against a glass wall."
- **Losing balance:** "Think train tracks, not a tightrope — feet should be hip-width apart, not in line."

---

## CURL (Barbell, Dumbbell, Cable)

### Execution
- **"Imagine your elbows are nailed to your sides — only your forearms move"** — eliminates swinging.
- "Squeeze the juice out of the orange at the top" — peak contraction.
- "Lower the weight like you're fighting gravity — 3 seconds down" — eccentric control.

### Common Mistakes
- **Swinging:** "If your body sways, lean your back against a wall."
- **Wrist curling:** "Your wrist is a steel rod — it doesn't bend."

---

## TRICEP EXTENSION (Overhead, Pushdown, Skull Crusher)

### Execution
- **"Lock your elbows in space — only your forearms swing like a door hinge"** — isolates triceps.
- "Squeeze the bar down and think about breaking it apart" — full lockout.
- "On overhead extensions, keep your biceps glued to your ears" — prevents flaring.

### Common Mistakes
- **Elbows flaring:** "Elbows face forward, always — tape them together mentally."

---

## GENERAL BRACING CUE (All Compound Lifts)

- "Big breath in through your nose — fill your belly 360° like a balloon."
- "Now brace like someone's about to punch you in the gut."
- "Hold that air through the hardest part of the rep. Exhale only at the top."
- This is called the **Valsalva maneuver** — it stabilizes the spine under heavy loads.

---

## TEMPO CUES (Universal)

| Cue | Meaning |
|-----|---------|
| "3-1-1" | 3 sec eccentric, 1 sec pause, 1 sec concentric |
| "Control the negative" | Slow, deliberate lowering phase |
| "Explode up" | Maximum intent on the concentric |
| "Own every inch" | Full range of motion under control |
